{{short description|Concept in mathematical logic}}
In [[mathematical logic]], '''indiscernibles''' are objects that cannot be distinguished by any [[property (philosophy)|property]] or [[relation (mathematics)|relation]] defined by a [[well-formed formula|formula]]. Usually only [[first-order logic|first-order]] formulas without [[Equality (mathematics)#In logic|equality]] are considered. 
==Examples==
If ''a'', ''b'', and ''c'' are [[Distinct (mathematics)|distinct]] and {''a'', ''b'', ''c''} is a '''[[Set (mathematics)|set]] of indiscernibles''', then, for example, for each binary formula <math> \beta </math>, we must have

:<math> [ \beta (a, b) \land \beta (b, a) \land \beta (a, c) \land \beta (c, a) \land \beta (b, c) \land \beta (c, b) ] \lor</math>

:<math>[ \lnot \beta (a, b) \land \lnot \beta (b, a) \land \lnot \beta(a, c) \land \lnot \beta (c, a) \land \lnot \beta (b, c) \land \lnot \beta (c, b) ] \,.</math>

Historically, the [[identity of indiscernibles]] was one of the [[laws of thought]] of [[Gottfried Leibniz]].

==Generalizations==
In some contexts one considers the more general notion of '''order-indiscernibles''', and the term '''sequence of indiscernibles''' often refers implicitly to this weaker notion. In our example of binary formulas, to say that the triple (''a'', ''b'', ''c'') of distinct elements is a sequence of indiscernibles implies

:<math> ( [ \varphi (a, b) \land \varphi (a, c) \land \varphi (b, c) ] \lor  [ \lnot \varphi (a, b) \land \lnot \varphi (a, c) \land \lnot \varphi (b, c) ] )</math> and
:<math>( [ \varphi (b, a) \land \varphi (c, a) \land \varphi (c, b) ] \lor  [ \lnot \varphi (b, a) \land \lnot \varphi (c, a) \land \lnot \varphi (c, b) ] ) \,.</math>

More generally, for a structure <math>\mathfrak A</math> with domain <math>A</math> and a linear ordering <math> < </math>, a set <math>I\subseteq A</math> is said to be a set of <math> < </math>-indiscernibles for <math>\mathfrak A</math> if for any finite subsets <math>\{i_0,\ldots,i_n\}\subseteq I</math> and <math>\{j_0,\ldots,j_n\}\subseteq I</math> with <math>i_0<\ldots<i_n</math> and <math>j_0<\ldots<j_n</math> and any first-order formula <math>\phi</math> of the language of <math>\mathfrak A</math> with <math>n</math> free variables, <math>\mathfrak A\vDash\phi(i_0,\ldots,i_n) \iff \mathfrak A\vDash\phi(j_0,\ldots,j_n)</math>.<ref>J. Baumgartner, F. Galvin, "[https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/0003484378900128 Generalized Erdős cardinals and 0<sup>#</sup>]". Annals of Mathematical Logic vol. 15, iss. 3 (1978).</ref><sup>p. 2</sup>

==Applications==
Order-indiscernibles feature prominently in the theory of [[Ramsey cardinal]]s, [[Erdős cardinal]]s, [[Silver cardinal]]s, and [[zero sharp]].
